newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's Hussein to meet PLO's Arafat in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Hussein to meet PLO's Arafat in West Bank.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein will travel to the West Bank on Tuesday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for his first visit to the region in 29 years, a senior PLO official said on Monday.
"King Hussein is returning to Jericho with Arafat where they will hold a meeting on Tuesday," the PLO official told Reuters.
King Hussein has not visited the West Bank since Israel seized the territory from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war.
It was not immediately clear whether U.S.-brokered Israeli-Palestinian peace talks slated to be held in Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba on Tuesday would be held as planned.
"We don't know whether we're going to Taba or not," Palestinian chief negotiator Saeb Erekat told Israel Channel One.

A Palestinian spokesman in Amman, where King Hussein and Arafat were meeting, said U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross would meet Arafat in the Jordanian capital later on Monday night to help in breaking the impasse.
Erekat was meeting his Israel counterpart Lieutenant-General Dan Shomron in informal talks at a Jerusalem hotel. When asked whether the talks had acheived progress, Erekat said: "No".
But Shomron said progress had been achieved.
"There is progress and a narrowing of positions all the time," he told the television.
Palestinian negotiators still planned to go to Taba on Tuesday.
"Our instructions are to head for Taba for talks with the Israelis on Tuesday after the Arafat-Hussein meeting" senior Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour told Reuters.
A PLO official had earlier reported the talks were off.
The formal Taba talks were to have resumed on Monday but were pushed back to allow the sides to progress in informal negotiation channels.
Arafat met King Hussein to brief him on talks over Israel's long-delayed redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron.
King Hussein called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a break in his talks with Arafat, Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti said without giving details.
